author: TEDx Talks
description:
Around the world, most people say living in a democracy matters to them — and most also say their democracy isn't working. Tamara Cofman Wittes thinks she knows why: we're practicing democracy too fast. Borrowing Kahneman's split between the fast, emotional mind and the slow, reasoning one, she argues that an attention economy built on conflict has pushed us to do all of our democracy in the reactive register. A viral clip is long enough to start a fight but far too short to change a mind — and "democracy fast," she warns, is a gift to leaders like Putin and Xi, who profit when a society stays angry and divided.

The hopeful turn is that the antidote is already in our hands. Drawing on her work with civic movements abroad, Wittes tells the stories of citizens in Malawi and Venezuela who slowed democracy back down to a human pace — ordinary people who, through patient preparation, drew a clear line between a lie and the truth at moments when an election could have tipped into chaos. Wh
title: Why politics feels overwhelming—and how to fix it | Tamara Cofman Wittes | TEDxMidAtlantic

description: In this insightful talk, Genevieve Richardson explores society's pressure to have answers, even when we are uncertain or lack sufficient understanding. She challenges the perception that uncertainty is a weakness, arguing instead that recognising what we do not know is an important part of intellectual curiosity and personal growth. Genevieve encourages us to embrace doubt without falling into apathy, question assumptions, and resist the temptation to confuse confidence with knowledge. Her message reminds us that sometimes the greatest step towards understanding is having the courage to say, "I don't know." author: TEDx Talks
description: In this thought-provoking talk, Joy Li uses the seemingly simple question, “Is a hot dog a sandwich?” to explore how we categorise, label, and define things, including ourselves. Drawing on her personal journey of identifying as an introvert and searching for a label that truly represented her, Joy challenges the need to fit into predefined identities. She invites us to move beyond asking, “Which label defines me?” and instead consider, “Why do I need a label at all?” Ultimately, her talk encourages us to embrace self-discovery, challenge limiting definitions, and recognise that who we are is not fixed but full of possibilities. Grade 10 student at Guanghou Foreign Languages School, China. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. description: In this talk, Serena Chen explores the dangers of procrastination, unhealthy work habits, and sacrificing sleep in the pursuit of academic success. Drawing from her personal experience of staying up late even when there was no homework left, she reflects on the misconception that working longer hours and feeling exhausted are signs of productivity and dedication. She challenges this belief by highlighting how sleep deprivation negatively affects concentration, memory, brain function, and physical health. Serena encourages students to rethink their approach to discipline, embrace effective time management, and recognise that adequate rest is not laziness but an essential part of achieving sustainable success. Join Paula Bontempi as she shares how scientists are like doctors - doing regular check-ups on Earth's vital signs—and why the results demand our presence, not just our concern. Paula Bontempi is a Professor of Oceanography at the University of Rhode Island’s Graduate School of Oceanography and served at NASA Headquarters as acting deputy director of the Earth Science Division and as a physical scientist and program manager in ocean biology and biogeochemistry. She served as NASA Program Scientist for instrument and mission science, including the Sea-Viewing Wide Field-of-View Sensor (SeaWiFS), Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (NPP), and the Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, Ocean Ecosystem (PACE) mission. description:
Gaps in communities exist. Some gaps are functional, while others are social.
After moving to a new town, Allison McEntee was eager to build her community and discovered that belonging wasn't something you find—it was something you build. Through discovering gaps in her community, she explores the overlooked roles of "Builders": the people who make change, take risks, persevere through criticism, and create the connections that bring communities together. In an era of increasing isolation and division, this talk is a call to stop waiting for someone else to fix what's missing and start building it yourself. In a world powered by data, AI, and endless scrolling, Allison believes human connection still matters most. Nine years ago, she founded the Kenilworth Cookbook Club to bring people together around food and conversation. What began at her kitchen table has grown into the nation’s largest network of Cookbook Clubs — creating spaces where strangers become friends and neighbors build

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Você realmente escolhe o que compra? Ou suas escolhas já foram influenciadas antes mesmo de você perceber?

O carro que dirigimos, a roupa que vestimos e as marcas que consumimos dizem muito mais do que imaginamos. Por trás de cada compra, podem existir desejos de pertencimento, reconhecimento e aceitação.

Nesta palestra, Roberto Mendes explora a arquitetura silenciosa do consumo e revela como o marketing, a publicidade e os padrões sociais influenciam não apenas nossas decisões, mas também a maneira como construímos nossa identidade.

Ao apresentar o conceito de “consumo da incompletude”, Roberto questiona por que buscamos em produtos e marcas respostas para necessidades que vão muito além do material.

Com referências ao filósofo Jean Baudrillard e ao paradoxo do barco de Teseu, ele mostra como padrões se transformam em hábitos, crenças e limites que passam a orientar nossas vidas quase sem que percebamos.

Mas existe uma questão ainda mais desconfortável: até que ponto somos respo
title: Você escolhe ou escolhem por você? | Roberto Mendes | TEDxPraça Getúlio Vargas

It sharpens focus, lifts mood, builds resilience, and brings back genuine joy when life feels heavy.

In a world that often prioritizes efficiency over well-being, she's passionate about showing that exercise is one of the most accessible tools for nurturing mental health—and that tending to our minds is essential, because neglecting them quietly impacts our bodies in profound ways. Through stories from the court, real science, and simple inspiration, she shares how embracing movement can help us all shine brighter, handle stress with grace, and thrive in body and mind.
